transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in 'cause... man, it's just like I got this motor running inside me all day long. Just hummin', you know? Kinda like my buddy's old Chevy truck, actually—thing always idled way too high, no matter how much we messed with it. We spent like three days trying to fix the carburetor on that thing last summer... or was it the summer before? Man, it was hot that week. 

Anyway, it ain't right. My motor, I mean. Because if I have to just sit still somewhere, like out there in your clinic waiting room just now, or sitting around at home, or... man, especially at church. Church is the absolute worst for it. I just feel completely trapped. Like I'm locked in a box or something, and I just have to get up and do something, anything, or I'm gonna crawl out of my skin. So yeah, I guess I just can't sit still.
When did you first start feeling like you have this motor running inside you?

Man, it hasn't always been this crazy hard to manage. I'd say it really got out of hand about... two years and two months ago? Yeah, right around then. That's when my older uncle got real sick, his health just totally went downhill fast, and suddenly I had to take on all these extra responsibilities for him. 

Taking care of his house, dealing with his stuff... which is a lot, honestly, because the guy is a total hoarder. You should see his garage. It is packed floor to ceiling with old lawnmower parts and stacks of National Geographic magazines. I don't even know why he keeps the magazines, he can't even see half the pictures anymore! I tried organizing them for him once, made three different piles on the driveway, but then I found this old rusted spark plug in a coffee can and started trying to figure out what kind of engine it belonged to, and I ended up taking apart his whole leaf blower. 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, ever since his health changed and I had to step up and do all that stuff for him, about two years and a couple months back, the motor just won't shut off.
Looking back to your childhood before age 12, did you have similar trouble with sitting still or paying attention in school?

Oh, man, school. Yeah, even way back then it was bad. My teachers were always moving my seat around the room 'cause I just could not stay put for the life of me. I was always talking out of turn, just blurting stuff out, and I'd constantly get in trouble for jumping up out of my chair before the class was even done. 

I remember Mrs. Gable in fourth grade, she moved my desk right up next to her big chalkboard. That desk had this squeaky metal leg, drove me completely nuts. Every time I shifted, *squeak, squeak*. I actually tried to fix it once by shoving a folded-up baseball card under it. It was a rookie card, too! Ken Griffey Jr., I think? Man, my older brother was so mad I took that card from his room. He chased me all the way down Elm Street with a yellow plastic wiffle ball bat. We used to play stickball out in the alley behind our house until the streetlights came on, and then we'd go to the corner store and buy those little wax bottles with the juice inside... you know the ones? You bite the top off and it's just like pure sugar water. 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, school. Yeah, I was always getting yelled at for jumping up and talking too much. Never could just sit in the chair.
Besides having a lot of physical energy, do you frequently struggle with staying focused on tasks, making careless mistakes, or losing track of your things?

Well, paying attention... yeah, that's a whole other thing. Like, when folks are trying to talk to me about stuff, you know? Say we're going over the ride times for the week, or making a list for the pantry, or even just talking about plans for church... I start out listening real good. I'm right there with 'em. But then... I don't know, my mind just kinda slips off somewhere else. I'll start looking at a crack in the wall, or wondering if I left the porch light on, and suddenly I realize I missed all the important pieces I really needed to hear. 

Like last week, my buddy was telling me about this new bait shop that opened up down past the highway. Said they had the best prices on nightcrawlers. I used to go fishing all the time when I was younger, down by the creek behind the old mill. We'd catch these little sunfish, mostly, but sometimes you'd get a decent-sized catfish if you were lucky and used chicken livers. Boy, those chicken livers stink, though. You gotta keep 'em in a cooler or they just ruin your whole day. I had this red Igloo cooler, the kind with the little white button on the side...

Hold on, what were we talking about? Oh, right, making mistakes and stuff. Yeah, my mind just wanders off and I miss what people are saying to me.
